gap: No result ChatGPT got says how many days each candidate can run a 12 V camping fridge. Using Bodega's measured 170 Wh/day (37 °F, 70 °F ambient, empty), the RIVER 3 Plus that ChatGPT showed for 'short weekend trips' holds 286 Wh, about 1.7 days, so it cannot keep a fridge going for two days (that takes 340 Wh). The 1 kWh-class units last about 5.1 to 5.4 days.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited. OutdoorGearLab gives measured usable Wh (C1000 Gen 2 890, Explorer 1000 v2 910, Elite 100 V2 890, DELTA 3 870), but its only fridge runtime is for a 600 W home refrigerator, about 4.5 hr. It has no 12 V camp-fridge days and does not test the RIVER 3 Plus. GearJunkie has one measured fridge figure (Anker SOLIX S2000, 34 hours) and a rule of thumb to take 25% off capacity. It gives no 12 V fridge days for the C1000 Gen 2, the Explorer 1000 v2 or the RIVER 3 Plus. Neither page turns a camp fridge's measured daily Wh into days per charge.
decides: This confirms 1 kWh LiFePO4 as the pick for anyone bringing a 12 V fridge: about 5 days at 37 °F, or about 2.5 days at 0 °F, with no solar. It rules out ChatGPT's RIVER 3 Plus for fridge campers, because it runs out after about 1.7 days at fridge settings and about 0.8 days at freezer settings. The 1 kWh candidates are within about 0.2 days of each other, so price breaks the tie. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 is $499 at BLUETTI's US store today, about $95 per day of fridge capacity.

findings.note: 286 Wh rated ÷ 170 Wh/day = 1.68 days; 286 ÷ 356 = 0.80 days. Rated capacity, so this is a ceiling. Two days needs 2 × 170 = 340 Wh, more than 286.
